title: Altered immune and metabolic molecular pathways drive islet cell dysfunction in human type 1 diabetes.
authors: Dos Santos, Theodore; Dai, Xiao-Qing; Jones, Robert C; Spigelman, Aliya F; Mummey, Hannah M; Ewald, Jessica D; Ellis, Cara E; Lyon, James G; Smith, Nancy; Bautista, Austin; Manning Fox, Jocelyn E; Neff, Norma F; Detweiler, Angela M; Tan, Michelle; Arrojo E Drigo, Rafael; Xia, Jianguo; Camunas-Soler, Joan; Gaulton, Kyle J; Quake, Stephen R; MacDonald, Patrick E
one_liner_zh: 该研究结合电生理、转录组和机器学习分析T1D胰岛细胞功能障碍，虽涉及转录因子定位但非蛋白质-DNA互作建模核心，方法无AI/物理模拟创新，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by the autoimmune destruction of most insulin-producing beta cells, along with dysregulated glucagon secretion from pancreatic alpha cells. We conducted an integrated analysis that combines electrophysiological and transcriptomic profiling, along with machine learning, of islet cells from T1D donors. The few surviving beta cells exhibit altered electrophysiological properties and transcriptomic signatures indicative of increased antigen presentation, metabolic reprogramming, and impaired protein translation. In alpha cells, we observed hyperresponsiveness and increased exocytosis, which are associated with upregulated immune signaling, disrupted transcription factor localization, and lysosome homeostasis, as well as dysregulation of mTORC1 complex signaling. Notably, key genetic risk signals for T1D were enriched in transcripts related to alpha cell dysfunction, including MHC class I, which were closely linked with alpha cell dysfunction. Our data provide what we believe are novel insights into the molecular underpinnings of islet cell dysfunction in T1D, highlighting pathways that may be leveraged to preserve residual beta cell function and modulate alpha cell activity. These findings underscore the complex interplay between immune signaling, metabolic stress, and cellular identity in shaping islet cell phenotypes in T1D.
abstract_zh: 1型糖尿病（T1D）的特征是大多数产生胰岛素的β细胞被自身免疫性破坏，同时胰腺α细胞的胰高血糖素分泌失调。我们对来自T1D供体的胰岛细胞进行了整合分析，结合了电生理和转录组学分析以及机器学习。少数存活的β细胞表现出改变的电生理特性和转录组特征，表明抗原呈递增加、代谢重编程和蛋白质翻译受损。在α细胞中，我们观察到过度反应和胞吐作用增强，这与免疫信号上调、转录因子定位紊乱、溶酶体稳态以及mTORC1复合物信号失调相关。值得注意的是，T1D的关键遗传风险信号富集在与α细胞功能障碍相关的转录本中，包括MHC I类，这些与α细胞功能障碍密切相关。我们的数据提供了我们认为对T1D胰岛细胞功能障碍分子基础的新见解，突出了可能用于保留残余β细胞功能和调节α细胞活性的通路。这些发现强调了免疫信号、代谢应激和细胞身份在塑造T1D胰岛细胞表型中的复杂相互作用。
